第468章 第四声回敲（第1页）
第四声回敲（第22页）空气里出现一股味道。不是消毒水，不是铁锈。是纸灰和海水混合的气味，干燥中带着咸腥，像有人在一座烧过的图书馆里倒了一桶海水。陈默低头看李主任的掌心。伤口没有愈合。三根黑线断裂的地方留下三道浅痕，但在掌心正中央，有一个规整的半圆——不是伤疤，是像用圆规画出来的弧线，边缘光滑得像瓷器断面。他转头看医护。医护的掌心也有一个半圆。方向不同，但弧度完全一致。陈默的喉咙发紧。“把灯打开。”旁边的医生愣了一下：“灯已经——”“全部打开。”隔离区的灯一盏接一盏亮起来。白光照在三个人的掌心上，影子投在墙上。陈默看见了三个半圆。他自己的右肩焦痕是弧线的一端，李主任的掌心是另一端，医护的掌心是第三段。三个半圆在灯光下连成一条完整的弧线——不是散落的碎片，是三个缺口刚好能拼成一个圆。像门环。陈默的脑子里嗡了一声。他刚才不是在救人。他是在帮门完成最后一道切割。三、门环在墙上合拢灯光在墙上晃了一下。陈默看见那个圆在墙上闭合了。三个半圆的投影在墙面相遇，边缘无缝对接，形成一个完整的环形。不是画上去的——是像烙铁烫进墙皮，线条从浅变深，从模糊变清晰。门环。墙上的投影变成了一个门环的形状，内侧开始凹陷，像有什么东西从墙的另一侧在往外推。监护仪响了。不是警报声。是敲击声。四台监护仪同时发出同一个声音——咚、咚、咚、咚。不是机器故障，是心跳监测的滴声变成了敲门声，从扬声器里传出来，节奏和刚才医护胸腔里的敲击一模一样。第四声。陈默盯着墙上的门环。环形的内侧开始浮现东西——不是纹路，不是图案，是一只眼睛。没有眼白。瞳孔占据了整个眼眶，黑得像能把光线吸进去。那只眼睛在门环内侧缓缓转动，像在扫描整个房间。每转一度，墙皮就剥落一片，露出下面的灰色水泥。陈默听见了呼吸声。不是自己的，不是李主任的，不是医生的。是墙里的呼吸——像有什么巨大的胸腔在墙体内部缓慢起伏，每一次吸气都让墙皮向内凹陷，每一次呼气都让墙皮向外鼓出。门后有人。不是“有人”——是有东西。它站在门后面，手已经搭在门环上，只差最后一下就能把门拉开。然后它说话了。“陈默。”声音从墙里传出来，不是通过空气传播，是直接震在骨头里。陈默的颅骨在共鸣，牙根在发酸，耳膜在向内凹陷。不是“雷诺”。是“陈默”。它叫的是他的本名。不是骑士的名字，不是穿越者的代号——是那个在现代考古队里被叫了三十年的名字。陈默的右手开始发抖。不是因为恐惧。是因为他听见了雷诺的心跳。胸腔里有两颗心脏在跳——一颗是自己的，一颗是雷诺残留的。两颗心脏在敲第四声的节奏，像在回应门后的呼唤。墙上的门环开始发光。不是圣光的冷白，是那种从内部透出来的暗红，像烧红的铁环在黑暗中缓慢冷却。门环内侧的那只眼睛在缩小，在向中心收拢，像瞳孔在强光下收缩。但它没有消失。它在聚焦。在锁定陈默。“它知道我的名字。”陈默的声音从喉咙里挤出来，干涩得不像自己的。旁边的医生张着嘴，说不出话。李主任靠在墙上，瞳孔里的黑点在扩散。监护仪的敲击声停了。四台机器同时归零。然后第四声回敲从墙里传出来——不是敲在门上，是敲在陈默的胸腔里。声音在肋骨之间回荡，在心脏瓣膜之间弹跳，最后收束到右肩焦痕的缺口里。陈默低头。右肩的焦痕在发光。和墙上的门环一样的光。暗红色，从皮肤下面透出来，像有一枚烧红的铁钉嵌在骨头里。他伸手去摸，指尖碰到焦痕边缘的瞬间，听见了一个声音——不是敲门声。是锁芯转动的声音。墙上的门环开始旋转。

Chapter 468 The Fourth Knock (Page 1)
The Fourth Knock Back (page 22) A smell fills the air. Not disinfectant, not rust. It's the smell of paper ash mixed with seawater, dry and salty, like someone poured a bucket of seawater into a burned library. Chen Mo lowered his head and looked at Director Li's palm. The wound did not heal. Three shallow marks were left where the three black lines broke, but in the center of the palm, there was a regular semicircle - not a scar, but an arc drawn with a compass, with edges as smooth as a porcelain cross section. He turned to the medical staff. There is also a semicircle in the doctor's palm. The directions are different, but the arcs are exactly the same. Chen Mo's throat tightened. "Turn on the lights." The doctor next to him was stunned for a moment: "The lights have been -" "Turn them all on." The lights in the isolation area lit up one after another. White light shines on the palms of the three people, casting shadows on the wall. Chen Mo saw three semicircles. The scorch mark on his own right shoulder is one end of the arc, Director Li's palm is the other end, and the doctor's palm is the third segment. The three semicircles formed a complete arc under the light—not scattered fragments, but three gaps that could just fit together to form a circle. Like a door knocker. Chen Mo's mind buzzed. He was not rescuing people just now. He was helping the door complete the final cut. 3. The door knocker closed on the wall and the light flickered on the wall. Chen Mo saw the circle closing on the wall. Three semicircular projections meet on the wall, and their edges are seamlessly connected to form a complete ring. It's not painted on - it's like a soldering iron burning into the wall, the lines changing from light to dark, from blur to clear. Knockers. The projection on the wall changed into the shape of a door knocker, and the inside began to dent, as if something was pushing out from the other side of the wall. The monitor rang. Not a siren. It's a knocking sound. The four monitors made the same sound at the same time - boom, boom, boom, boom. It wasn't a machine malfunction, but the beeping sound of the heartbeat monitor turned into a knock on the door, coming from the speaker. The rhythm was exactly the same as the tapping in the doctor's chest just now. The fourth tone. Chen Mo stared at the door knocker on the wall. Something began to appear on the inside of the ring—not a pattern, not a pattern, but an eye. No whites of eyes. The pupils took up the entire eye socket, and were so black that they seemed to be able to suck in light. The eye moved slowly on the inside of the door knocker, as if scanning the entire room. With every degree of rotation, a piece of the wall peels off, revealing the gray cement underneath. Chen Mo heard breathing. It's not mine, not Director Li's, not the doctor's. It's the breathing in the wall - like some huge chest rising and falling slowly inside the wall. Every inhalation makes the wall skin dent inward, and every exhalation makes the wall skin bulge outward. There is someone behind the door. It’s not “someone” – it’s something. It stood behind the door, its hand already on the door knocker, just one last push away from pulling the door open. Then it spoke. "Chen Mo." The voice came from the wall, not through the air, but directly vibrating in the bones. Chen Mo's skull was resonating, his teeth were getting sore, and his eardrums were sinking inwards. Not "Renault". It's "Chen Mo". It was called by his real name. It's not the name of a knight, not the code name of a time traveler - it's the name that has been called by the modern archaeological team for thirty years. Chen Mo's right hand began to tremble. Not out of fear. It was because he heard Renault's heartbeat. There were two hearts beating in his chest - one was his own, and the other was what was left of Renault. Two hearts beating the fourth beat, as if responding to the call behind the door. The door knocker on the wall began to glow. It's not the cold white of the holy light, but the dark red that shines from the inside, like a red-hot iron ring slowly cooling in the darkness. inside door knockerThe eye was shrinking, constricting toward the center, like a pupil constricting under bright light. But it hasn't gone away. It's focusing. Locking Chen Mo. "It knows my name." Chen Mo's voice came out of his throat, too dry to be his own. The doctor next to him opened his mouth and was speechless. Director Li leaned against the wall, the black spots in his pupils spreading. The tapping sound of the monitor stopped. Four machines reset to zero at the same time. Then the fourth knock came from the wall - not on the door, but on Chen Mo's chest. The sound echoed between the ribs, bounced between the heart valves, and finally converged into the scorched gap in the right shoulder. Chen Mo lowered his head. The scorch marks on his right shoulder were glowing. The same light as the knocker on the wall. Dark red, showing through from under the skin, like a red-hot iron nail embedded in the bone. He reached out to touch it, and the moment his fingertips touched the edge of the scorch mark, he heard a sound—it wasn't a knock on the door. It's the sound of the lock cylinder rotating. The knocker on the wall began to spin.
